notes: All five open questions answered from the full text. (1) Intradermal prilocaine mean times to full recovery: 76.3, 71.8 and 87.8 min at the three concentrations (78.6 min pooled, n=81), 32 min to 50% recovery; lignocaine was NOT injected in the same subjects on the same day - the paper ran two separate double-blind trials in different subject groups, with only seven subjects overlapping. (2) Yes, durations in minutes are given for every agent by two endpoints, so it is a human head-to-head skin measurement in minutes, not a ranking. (3) Volume was 0.1 ml per intradermal injection for every solution in both trials, and the tabulated endpoint is time to FULL recovery (a permanent score of 10 on pinprick over the bleb), with times to 50% recovery read off the curves as well; bupivacaine 82.5, mepivacaine 98.6 pooled, prilocaine 78.6 pooled, lignocaine 65.7, aptocaine 91.3 pooled. (4) Yes - intradermal bupivacaine was timed to complete recovery at 0.1 ml, 82.5 +/- 8.7 min, n=28. (5) Mepivacaine reached 97.0, 95.2 and 103.7 min to full recovery (98.6 pooled); nothing near 2.5 h, and the paper reports no significant difference in duration between concentrations, so a higher concentration cannot reach it either. Same-subject head-to-heads, settled: trial 1 = lignocaine + bupivacaine + aptocaine in the same 28 subjects; trial 2 = mepivacaine + prilocaine + aptocaine in the same 27. Only aptocaine crosses the two trials.
